label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: Clicking a category link gave no sign that the page was changing; the tree stayed identical for a step, so I could not tell whether the click worked and had to re-read.
The product grid is made of hundreds of empty status regions with no text, so there was no usable content and only unlabeled loading placeholders were perceived.

Every product has a link whose name is just title-link, a bare Toggle wishlist button, and a Choose variant button with no product name, so the same names repeat dozens of times and cannot be told apart.

The size and add-to-bag controls appear twice (page and sticky bar) with identical names, and the color group has swatch buttons without a clear selected state, so I had to guess which [name] a la bolsa to use.

The cart popup said Subtotal 0.00 right after adding and its [name] para [name] button was disabled, and the page did not move to the cart or confirm the add other than a count badge; the language also mixes [name] and [name] throughout.
The checkout page first showed only an empty header and a heading for two reads before the form appeared, with no loading message, so it looked broken.
